 341:     bindProject(binding: StatsProjectBinding) {
 342:         const projectKey = `${binding.project.id}:${binding.project.branch}`
 343:         if (projectKey !== this.projectKey) this.clear()
 344:         this.projectKey = projectKey
 345:         this.binding = binding
 346:     }
 347: 
 348:     clear() {
 349:         this.loadRevision += 1
 350:         this.binding = null
 351:         this.cards = []
 352:         this.isOpen = false
 353:         this.projectKey = null
 354:         this.source = null
 355:         projectUsageMetricsService.clear()
 356:         this.publish({ ...INITIAL_SNAPSHOT, controls: this.snapshot.controls })
 357:     }
 358: 
 359:     async open(cards: StatsCardDescriptor[]) {
 360:         if (!this.binding) throw new Error('Project stats are not bound to a project')
 361:         this.cards = cards
 362:         this.isOpen = true
 363:         await this.load(this.binding)
 364:     }
 365: 
 366:     setControls(changes: Partial<StatsControls>) {
 367:         const controls = { ...this.snapshot.controls, ...changes }
 368:         validateRangeTimestamp(controls.startUtc, 'startUtc')
 369:         validateRangeTimestamp(controls.endUtc, 'endUtc')
 370:         if (controls.startUtc && controls.endUtc && Date.parse(controls.startUtc) > Date.parse(controls.endUtc)) {
 371:             throw new Error('Stats start date must not be after end date')
 372:         }
 373:         if (!this.source) {
 374:             this.publish({ ...this.snapshot, controls })
 375:             return
 376:         }
 377: 
 378:         this.publish(buildSnapshot(this.source, controls))
 379:     }
 380: 
 381:     handleRepositoryChange(event: ProjectWatchEvent) {
 382:         const binding = this.binding
 383:         if (!binding || !this.isOpen) return
 384:         const path = normalizePath(event.path)
 385:         const usageMetricsPath = normalizePath(`${binding.config.projectFolder}/usage_metrics.csv`)
 386:         if (path !== usageMetricsPath && !recognizedActivityPath(path, binding.config)) return
 387: 
 388:         void this.load(binding)
 389:     }
 390: 
 391:     private async load(binding: StatsProjectBinding) {
 392:         const revision = ++this.loadRevision
 393:         this.publish({ ...this.snapshot, error: null, rows: [], status: 'loading' })
 394:         try {
 395:             const repositoryFiles = await binding.storage.listRepositoryFiles(binding.project)
 396:             if (revision !== this.loadRevision || binding !== this.binding) return
 397:             if (!binding.storage.loadTextFile) throw new Error('Repository text file loading is not available')
 398:             const { activityPaths } = findStatsSourcePaths(repositoryFiles, binding.config)
 399:             const activityFiles = await Promise.all(activityPaths.map(async (path) => {
 400:                 const file = await binding.storage.loadTextFile?.(binding.project, path)
 401:                 if (!file) throw new Error(`Activity file could not be loaded: ${path}`)
 402:                 const origin = activityOriginFromPath(path)
 403:                 if (!origin) throw new Error(`Invalid activity path: ${path}`)
 404: 
 405:                 return parseActivityFile(file.content, origin)
 406:             }))
 407:             const usageMetrics = await projectUsageMetricsService.load(
 408:                 binding.project,
 409:                 binding.config.projectFolder,
 410:                 binding.storage,
 411:                 repositoryFiles,
 412:             )
 413:             if (revision !== this.loadRevision || binding !== this.binding) return
 414: 
 415:             this.source = {
 416:                 activity: activityFiles,
 417:                 cards: this.cards,
 418:                 tokenRows: usageMetrics.tokenRows,
 419:                 tokenTimeAvailable: usageMetrics.available,
 420:                 warnings: usageMetrics.warnings,
 421:             }
 422:             this.publish(buildSnapshot(this.source, this.snapshot.controls))
 423:         } catch (error) {
 424:             if (revision !== this.loadRevision || binding !== this.binding) return
 425:             const normalizedError = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error))
 426:             this.source = null
 427:             this.publish({ ...this.snapshot, error: normalizedError, rows: [], status: 'error' })
 428:         }
 429:     }
 430: 
 431:     private publish(snapshot: ProjectStatsSnapshot) {
 432:         this.snapshot = snapshot
 433:         this.dispatchEvent(new Event('changed'))
 434:     }
 435: }

The stats data is built **on demand when the Stats view opens**, not when the project loads.

- Project loading only binds the service to the project/config/storage: [project_loading.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev2/app/src/services/project/project_loading.ts:219).
- Switching to Stats triggers `projectStatsService.open(cards)`: [stats_view.tsx](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev2/app/src/components/stats_view/stats_view.tsx:23).
- `open()` then reads the repository activity files and usage metrics and builds the snapshot: [project_stats_service.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2_workers/dev2/app/src/services/stats/project_stats_service.ts:359).

One nuance: after Stats has been opened once, `isOpen` remains true until the project is cleared. Relevant repository changes therefore rebuild the stats even while another view is displayed. Returning to Stats also calls `open()` and reloads them again. So it is initially lazy/on-demand, then kept refreshed for the remainder of that project session.

If post-integration synchronization fails, report the partial failure and keep the card assigned.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Add desktop Git and bridge regression tests. Existing renderer subscription should update without component-local state.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## acceptance criteria\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Successful integration immediately removes the outgoing indicator and disables `Integrate into project`.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Card integration finishes with no outgoing or incoming indicator and disables both integration and update actions.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Reopening the selector or waiting for polling is unnecessary.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- A second integration is not required to correct the icon and is unavailable when no outgoing changes remain.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Card and project integrations publish correct final worktree status; failure behavior remains unchanged.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n===== B_81_new_card_markdown_typing_lag.md =====\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nauthor:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nid: B_81\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\ninternalId: 8e4a295a-8788-4232-8be7-c97f5a1cf5c8\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\ntitle: new card Markdown typing lag\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nstatus: ready\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nowner:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\naffects:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nagents:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\npolicy:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nafter: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Problem\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nTyping in the **New card** description editor has noticeable input lag.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nPerformance trace `Trace-20260731T140458.json` records five input events that each block the renderer main thread for 52-64 ms. Layout and paint are small; synchronous React work consumes most of the time.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Cause\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n`NewCardDialog` passes `handleBodyChange` to `MarkdownEditor.onLiveChange`. Every editor change calls `setBody`, rerendering the complete dialog and the MDXEditor subtree. This also recreates the Markdown editor plugin array and many MUI elements and style objects. Development-mode React work and garbage collection amplify the cost.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThis bypasses the lifetime-stable editor approach already used by `CardEditor` and `CardBodyEditor`. `MarkdownEditor` already buffers local edits and exposes `getMarkdown`, `setMarkdown`, and `flush`; normal typing does not need to propagate the full body into parent React state.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Required change\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Keep the new-card Markdown editor lifetime-stable while typing, following `CardEditor` and `CardBodyEditor`.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Do not store the full Markdown body in `NewCardDialog` state on every keystroke.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Read the current body from the editor when submitting, checking whether the draft is dirty, and inserting or clearing the template.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Preserve existing template behavior: untouched template can be cleared; editing it changes the action back to `Template`; inserting then appends without discarding text.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Keep reset, cancel confirmation, `Ctrl+Enter`, and target-column behavior unchanged.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Do not change shared `MarkdownEditor` buffering semantics solely for this dialog.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Acceptance criteria\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Typing in the new-card description does not rerender `NewCardDialog` or remount/rerender the Markdown editor for every keystroke.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Submitted card body exactly matches current editor content.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Cancel confirmation detects description-only edits.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Template insert, clear, edit, and append behavior remains unchanged.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Opening, closing, successful creation, and project changes reset the draft correctly.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- [ ] A regression test verifies repeated description edits do not repeatedly render the editor boundary.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Existing new-card dialog and Markdown editor tests pass.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n===== B_82_orphaned_git_for_windows_processes.md =====\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nauthor:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nid: B_82\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\ninternalId: d97a054f-5a67-47bb-9070-df874cf9148e\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\ntitle: agent runs leave orphaned Git for Windows processes\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nstatus: ready\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nowner:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\naffects:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nagents:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\npolicy:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nafter: 7bdf27fc-963c-4545-83e2-93410e67f0e3\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Problem\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nAgent runs launched through MDÂ² can leave multiple `git.exe` processes running indefinitely. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Current implementation\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Investigation plan\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Required change\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Acceptance criteria\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n===== History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n===== F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nauthor: \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nid: F_96\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nstatus: ready\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nowner: \\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\naffects:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nagents:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\npolicy:\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n# Current state\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Current implementation\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Investigation plan\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Required change\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\\\\\\\r\\\\\\\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must title: Fix broken activity files.

---
Currently, when the system loads the activity files and there is a problem, like an old version it cant load, the app shows an error and doesnt fix it. So next time project opens, same error. 

Better if the app tries to fix things:

* If agent ref in card cant be found, remove ref from card.
* If old version, load as much as possible, revert to defaults otherwise.

If this needs to be done, make certain that saving and commiting the changes is done in 1 batch.

## Current state

- Activity version 4 parsing is strict. `migrateActivityValue` recognizes versions 1â€“3, but its final strict parse rejects the whole file when one required field, collection entry, permission combination, conversation link, or legacy shape is invalid. Migration therefore does not recover partially valid legacy files.
- Local Electron writes a successfully migrated activity file during read, outside the renderer's Git commit batch. GitHub reads activity files with the strict current-version parser and does not migrate them. Remote control inherits Electron behavior. Repair behavior therefore differs by storage backend.
- `AgentIntegration` loads every card `agents` reference independently. A missing file, malformed activity, missing conversation, or wrong-card conversation becomes a warning, but the unresolved reference remains in card frontmatter. Reopening project repeats same failure.
- `CommitBatcher` can put card Markdown and raw JSON writes in one `StorageService.commit`, but project loading has no activity-repair phase that collects both kinds of change before committing.

## implementation details

- Add one shared activity repair function beside strict parsing. Repair means producing canonical current-version activity from parseable fields while preserving each independently valid item. An independently valid item satisfies its own schema and required links; invalid nested items are dropped at smallest level that leaves their parent meaningful. If parent can no longer satisfy schema, drop parent.
- For old versions, apply known version transformations before tolerant normalization. Default missing or invalid top-level `actionSettings`, `conversations`, and `records` to empty collections. Normalize each action setting, conversation, conversation entry, record, and commit independently; preserve valid items and current defaults, and discard unrecoverable items. Revalidate record-to-conversation links after repair and discard records whose required links do not resolve.
- If JSON or root object cannot be parsed, replace file with empty canonical activity when origin can be derived from recognized `project.json` or `card__<internalId>.json` filename. If origin cannot be established, leave file unchanged and treat its references as unresolved. Do not rewrite a future schema version: future means version greater than current version, whose fields this app cannot safely interpret.
- Run repair after full project cards and repository file index load, before attaching persisted conversations. Group references by activity path and load each distinct file once. Include project activity file when present.
- After repair, retain a card reference only when its path loaded, its conversation exists, and conversation `cardInternalId` equals card `internalId`. Remove reference after any unresolved outcome, including missing file, malformed JSON, unrecoverable activity, missing conversation, or wrong-card conversation.
- Collect every changed activity JSON and every card whose references changed. Mutate agent references through canonical `Card` ownership, schedule raw activity files and card references together, then explicitly flush one `CommitBatcher` batch. Defer automatic flush while collecting repairs so no subset can commit early. One batch means one `StorageService.commit` request and one Git commit containing all repair writes for that project load.
- Remove Electron's read-time migration write. Local Electron, GitHub, and remote-control projects must use same shared repair and normal storage commit path. Normal manual/automatic push behavior remains unchanged.
- If repair commit fails, keep batch pending for retry, report one user-visible error, and do not issue a partial repair commit. Keep successfully repaired in-memory data usable during current project session.
- Add shared repair tests, project-load integration tests, storage-backend contract tests, and regression tests for partial legacy data, malformed current data, malformed JSON, future versions, wrong ownership, missing references, one-batch persistence, commit failure, and clean reopen.

## acceptance criteria

- Given a version 1, 2, or 3 activity containing valid and invalid items, project load produces canonical version 4 data: valid items remain, invalid items are dropped at smallest safe level, and missing collections use current empty defaults.
- Given malformed current-version activity, same tolerant repair rules apply. Given unparseable JSON with origin derivable from recognized filename, file becomes empty canonical current-version activity.
- Given future activity version, file is not rewritten because current app cannot safely interpret its schema.
- After repair, every retained card `agents` reference resolves to existing conversation owned by that card. Every unresolved reference is removed, regardless of failure cause.
- One project load with any number of repaired activity files and cards creates exactly one `StorageService.commit` request containing all changed files. No repair file is written or committed before complete batch is ready.
- When no activity content or card reference changes, project load creates no repair commit.
- When repair commit fails, no partial repair commit exists, pending batch remains retryable, and user sees one clear error.
- After successful repair, reopening project does not repeat repaired migration or missing-reference errors.
- Local Electron, GitHub, and remote-control storage produce same repaired content and reference cleanup.
- Unaffected activity data, card fields, conversation loading, commit history, push mode, and project loading remain unchanged.
